newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes draw interest amid high runs, storm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes draw interest amid high runs, storm.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes, especially light sweet grades, retained favor with Gulf refiners due to continuing thirst for distillates and current high output.
And domestic grades turned higher as a result of refinery buying due to the prospect of critical delays in crude tanker shipments and loss of Gulf production, because of the storm.
"A huge chunk of supplies were lost, even for a day or so, and nobody wants to wait until the actuals are known," an East Coast trader said.
Some traders estimated that 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) could have been lost over the brief shut-ins.
The narrow import abitrage at $1.00 a barrel for November West Texas Intermediate/Brent stayed prohibitive, forcing most refiners to turn to domestic alternatives.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James rose five cents to 50 cents premium over WTI, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire also rose about eight cents to 27 cents premium.
Heavy sours fared less vigorously, dampened by more ample Latin American supplies, but also managed to inch higher.
West Texas Sour/Midland firmed slightly to minus $1.30, and Eugene Island also firmed to minus $1.09.
Foreign grades were scarce with Brent sellers not showing firm numbers due to poor arbitrage economics.
Traders were still pegging last deals at WTI plus 10-15 cents cif, with up to two million barrels rumored traded last week to two seperate refiners.
Cusiana was seen offered for early Nov at Dec WTI plus 15 cents, while Oriente for mid-November was talked around WTI minus $2.00 cif, traders said.
